title: Navimower 0.4.4-beta19

## Restore European cartographic alignment

- Re-enable the experimental EPSG:8366 ITRF2014-like -> ETRF2014 / ETRS89 cartographic translation for qualifying European vendor/static map georeferences.
- Keep the beta17/beta18 WGS84 ellipsoid metre conversion and persisted-state migration. The cartographic translation is now applied only after that ellipsoid georeference pipeline is complete.
- Preserve local mower/map geometry: local X/Y, zone polygons, dock geometry, charging-pile `position` / `nav_pos`, rotation and scale are not modified. Only the absolute WGS84 reference used to place the whole map on the basemap is translated.
- Continue excluding X3 when its `x3_rtk_anchor` / vendor RTK-bias path owns the absolute translation, so the ETRS89 correction is never stacked on top of the X3 vendor correction.

## Why it is back

- beta17 deliberately disabled the beta16 cartographic correction so fresh H2/i1/i2/X3 evidence could be collected in the vendor geographic frame while the spherical metre model was replaced.
- beta18 ensured no old spherical fit could survive the migration. Fresh Estonia field evidence now again shows a common roughly one-metre south-west / clock-7 displacement against static orthophoto on the H2/i1-style path, matching the magnitude and direction of the EPSG:8366 correction near Estonia.
- i1/i108 also shows a separate vendor-static versus cloud/GPS reference disagreement. beta19 does not hide or hard-code that residual; it restores only the common cartographic-frame translation so the remaining i1-specific component can be measured independently.

## Field test

- Compare H2/Tont and i1/i108 against the same orthophoto after updating. The whole mower + zones + dock group should move together; mower position relative to its own local map must remain unchanged.
- For i1/i108, record the remaining direction and distance after the common ETRS89 shift. Do not add a model-specific offset yet.
- X3 should remain unchanged by this beta. i2 receives the correction only when its active map has the same qualifying vendor/static georeference evidence; no model-name hard-code is used.
